findings.title: Cross-site GET can trigger TMS token deletion
findings.problem: GET /v1/user/log_out, resolved from the session credential alone with no CSRF token, Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site check, now also deletes every stored MCP and tool OAuth token of that user. Before this change the same request only cleared the session cookie. The fix-up gates the purge on _is_same_site_request (user.py:187) and tests it, but fix_evidence maps CR-003 to a bare decision string, not a decision object with outcome and rationale, so no recorded human decision exists for whether cross-site-initiated logout should purge tokens.
findings.impact: Without a recorded decision the gate is an unapproved behavior choice: same-site-only purge leaves TMS tokens in place for header-less, cross-site or metadata-less logouts (for example IdP-initiated links or browsers that send none of Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin or Referer).
findings.recommendation: Record the human's call as fix_evidence CR-003 decision {outcome, rationale}: keep the same-origin/same-site gate as implemented, or choose another rule. The gate itself needs no further code change unless the decision differs.

finding_status.notes: logout_token_cleanup.remove_user_tokens_on_logout_async bounds to_thread with wait_for and LOGOUT_TOKEN_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (config 5.0); both routes call it and the GET user lookup is wrapped in wait_for. Timeout tests exist. Residual: worker thread is uncancellable; lower-layer timeouts are out of scope.

No production change; test_user_router.py drives the real IdpFactory/JwksValidatingIdp chain: purge runs with proxy-injected headers (JWKS on and off) and cookie-only or Bearer-less JWKS requests are explicitly asserted as skipped, which the finding allowed. Tests use importorskip, so execution is left to Stage 7.

fix_evidence CR-003 decision is a bare string, not {outcome, rationale}, and nothing shows a human made the call; source cannot resolve a decision finding. The same-site gate (user.py:187) and its tests are present.

from __future__ import annotations present after the docstring in logout_token_cleanup.py, test_logout_token_cleanup.py, test_logout_token_cleanup_mock_tms.py and the new thread_safe_ttl_cache modules.

remove_user_tokens_on_logout runs the delete and each purge under _attempt, logging class name only, so one failure neither skips another purge nor hides the delete failure. OIDC _cache and TMSTokenStore._fallback are ThreadSafeTTLCache; every access in both classes uses its locked get, set, pop or purge_prefix.
